newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re repeats forecast for good 1997.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re repeats forecast for good 1997.

text.p: Swiss Re reiterated forecasts that 1997 profit would develop positively and that gross premiums could rise by as much as 25 percent.

"We expect the generally satisfactory business performance of early 1997, further improvements in the balance sheet structure and the expansion of the scope of consolidation to have a positivve impact on the result." Swiss Re said in a letter to shareholders released at the annual meeting.
Chief Executive Walter Kielholz said business had been good thus far and he reiterated an outlook that 1997 premiums could grow by up to a quarter.

"Business has been favourable up until now. We expect premiums to rise strongly by 20 to 25 percent, with this growth coming mainly from the acquisition of Mercantile & General Re," he said in the text of a speech to shareholders.
Swiss Re had a 1996 net profit after minorities of 1.46 billion Swiss francs. Its gross premiums totaled 14.2 billion.
